- Description of how cross-border flows are handled end-to-end (routing, regions, fallbacks).
- Sample operational logs showing anonymized request/response metadata (timestamps, region, model id, request id). Do logs include originating IPs?

- Any DPA Annex or DPF evidence bundle you can share for our legal team.

We would like the package by close of business on Friday (6/22) to stay on track. I've attached our standard RFI form for completeness.

Appreciate your help — please loop in whoever owns operational evidence and legal redlines.

Subject: Operational logs & controls — evidence bundle (draft)

Elena / Lauren — attaching our draft Operational Controls bundle that maps to the DPF categories you asked about. Highlights below and notes on the sample logs attached.

Key operational controls (summary):
- Cross-region routing: traffic is routed to customer-configured region shards. We provide region pins and automatic fallbacks only to approved regions; fallback policy is configurable per-customer.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. Customer data keys are stored in a customer-separate KMS namespace where available; control-plane credentials are isolated and rotated monthly.
- KMS/HSM: We leverage cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys for root signing; customer tenant keys can be integrated via BYOK where requested.
- Access & audit logs: request_id, timestamp (UTC), servicing_region, model_version, token_count, request_size_bytes, response_size_bytes, actor_principal_id.
- IP handling: By default we record origin IP in access logs; we can provide a pseudo-anonymized sample (IP hashed via salted HMAC) if you require.
- Retention: default access log retention = 90 days; extended retention plans (180/365 days) available under contract. Backup snapshots are retained for 30 days and subject to secure-delete policies.

Attachments included here: redwood_dpf_operational_controls_v1.pdf and s3_access_logs_sample.txt (redacted/pseudo-anonymized). The sample log includes the fields above and a note about hash salt handling.

If you need logs with full IPs for compliance review, we'll need an approved DPA Annex and a narrow-scoped access request from your compliance team (we can provide a temporary S3 share with time-limited access).

-Marcus
Head of Infra Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpf_operational_controls_v1.pdf, s3_access_logs_sample.txt

These records are included in the audit log tier (retained for 90 days by default); we can extend retention for audit records under contract.
